title: The inverse image of abelian sheaves along a morphism of sites is exact
statement: Let $f:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ be a morphism of sites given by the continuous functor $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (3), and let $f^{-1}=u_s:\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)\to\textit{Ab}(\mathcal D)$ be the inverse image on abelian sheaves, the left adjoint of $f_*=u^s$ on abelian sheaves. Then $f^{-1}$ is an additive functor which commutes with finite limits and finite colimits of $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$; in particular it carries kernels and cokernels to kernels and cokernels, short exact sequences $0\to\mathcal A\to\mathcal B\to\mathcal E\to0$ of $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ to short exact sequences of $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal D)$, and every exact sequence (finite or infinite, e.g. $0\to\mathcal A\to\mathcal I^0\to\mathcal I^1\to\cdots$) to an exact sequence.

source.place: Modules on Sites, Lemma Tag 04JC (lemma-flat-pullback-exact), first assertion and the first paragraph of its proof (the underlying sheaf of sets of the abelian f^{-1}G is the set-theoretic f^{-1} of the underlying sheaf of sets, Sites Section Tag 00YR, so exactness of f^{-1} on sheaves of sets gives exactness on abelian sheaves); stated there for a morphism of topoi, which a morphism of sites induces (Sites, Lemma Tag 00XC, lemma-morphism-sites-topoi); Lemma Tag 03DC (lemma-exactness-pushforward-pullback) for the colimits (left adjoint)

proof.text: *(1) What the definition gives.* By [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (3), $f$ is given by a continuous functor $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ such that $L:=u_s:\Sh(\mathcal C)\to\Sh(\mathcal D)$ on sheaves of sets is exact, i.e. commutes with finite limits and finite colimits (Sites, Definition 00X1); in particular $L$ sends the final sheaf $*$ to a final sheaf and binary products to binary products: $\lambda_{X,Y}=\langle L\mathrm{pr}_1,L\mathrm{pr}_2\rangle:L(X\times Y)\to LX\times LY$ is an isomorphism. $L$ is left adjoint to $R:=u^s$, $\mathcal G\mapsto\mathcal G\circ u$, on sheaves of sets, and the abelian $f^{-1}=u_s$ is left adjoint to the abelian $f_*=u^s$, $\mathcal G\mapsto\mathcal G\circ u$ (sectionwise group structure) [lem-weil-pbc-site-continuous-pushforward-sheaf], [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction]. This is an instance of the definitions.

*(2) The abelian $f^{-1}$ is computed on underlying sheaves of sets.* By [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-algebraic-structures-objects], on $\mathcal C$ and on $\mathcal D$, abelian sheaves are, compatibly with the forgetful functors $|-|$ to sheaves of sets, the abelian group objects $(\mathcal F,+,0,i)$ of $\Sh(-)$ (finite products in $\Sh(-)$ being sectionwise), and morphisms of abelian sheaves are the morphisms of sheaves of sets commuting with $+,0,i$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-lifts-group-ring-objects] to $L\dashv R$ (step 1; $L$ preserves finite products): $L$ and $R$ lift to an adjunction $L^{\mathrm{gr}}\dashv R^{\mathrm{gr}}$ between abelian sheaves, with $|L^{\mathrm{gr}}\mathcal G|=L|\mathcal G|$, $|L^{\mathrm{gr}}\varphi|=L|\varphi|$, group law $+_{L^{\mathrm{gr}}\mathcal G}=L(+_{\mathcal G})\circ\lambda^{-1}$, zero $L(0)\circ\lambda_*^{-1}$, negation $L(i)$. Since products in $\Sh(\mathcal C)$ are sectionwise and $(R\mathcal G)(V)=\mathcal G(u(V))$, the comparison $\rho$ of $R$ is the identity on sections and $R(+_{\mathcal G})$ is, on $V$-sections, the addition of $\mathcal G(u(V))$; so $R^{\mathrm{gr}}\mathcal G$ is $\mathcal G\circ u$ with its sectionwise group law, i.e. $R^{\mathrm{gr}}$ is the abelian $f_*=u^s$ of step 1, on objects and on morphisms. Both $f^{-1}$ and $L^{\mathrm{gr}}$ are thus left adjoints of the same functor $f_*$ on abelian sheaves, so by [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] (with $\delta=\mathrm{id}$) there is a natural isomorphism $c:f^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}L^{\mathrm{gr}}$ of functors $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)\to\textit{Ab}(\mathcal D)$ (this is the identification of Sites, Section 00YR and Proposition 00YV (2), recorded in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (3)). Each property in the statement (additivity; carrying limit cones of finite diagrams to limit cones, and colimit cocones of finite diagrams to colimit cocones; carrying exact sequences to exact sequences) holds for a functor if it holds for a naturally isomorphic one: $c$ transports cones, cocones and sequences to isomorphic ones, and $f^{-1}(\varphi)=c^{-1}_{\mathcal H}\circ L^{\mathrm{gr}}(\varphi)\circ c_{\mathcal G}$ is additive in $\varphi$ if $L^{\mathrm{gr}}$ is. So it suffices to prove steps 3-6 for $F:=L^{\mathrm{gr}}$, except that colimits (step 4) are treated for $f^{-1}$ directly.

source.place: Modules on Sites, proof of Lemma Tag 04JC (lemma-flat-pullback-exact), first paragraph ('the underlying sheaf of sets of f^{-1}G is the same as f^{-1} of the underlying sheaf of sets of G, see Sites, Section sheaves-algebraic-structures'), with Sites (sites.tex) Section Tag 00YR and Proposition Tag 00YV (2) and the discussion before it

proof.text: *(3) $F$ commutes with finite limits.* Let $M:\mathcal J\to\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$, $j\mapsto\mathcal G_j$, be a diagram indexed by a finite category with a limit cone $(\Lambda,(\pi_j)_j)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact] (1) the limit of abelian sheaves is computed sectionwise, so for every $U$ the cone $(\Lambda(U),(\pi_{j,U})_j)$ is a limit cone of abelian groups; the underlying set of a limit of abelian groups is the limit of the underlying sets (the set of compatible families with the componentwise operations), so $(|\Lambda|(U),(|\pi_j|_U)_j)$ is a limit cone of sets for every $U$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise] (2) $(|\Lambda|,(|\pi_j|)_j)$ is a limit cone of $|M|$ in $\Sh(\mathcal C)$. As $L$ commutes with finite limits (step 1), $(L|\Lambda|,(L|\pi_j|)_j)=(|F\Lambda|,(|F\pi_j|)_j)$ (step 2) is a limit cone of $L\circ|M|=|F\circ M|$ in $\Sh(\mathcal D)$; by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise] (2) again, for every object $W$ of $\mathcal D$ the map $(F\Lambda)(W)\to\lim_j(F\mathcal G_j)(W)$, $s\mapsto((F\pi_j)_W(s))_j$, is bijective. It is a homomorphism of abelian groups (each $(F\pi_j)_W$ is one), hence an isomorphism onto the limit of abelian groups, so $((F\Lambda)(W),((F\pi_j)_W)_j)$ is a limit cone of abelian groups for every $W$. Let $(\Lambda',(\pi'_j)_j)$ be the sectionwise limit of $F\circ M$, a limit in $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal D)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact] (1); the morphism $F\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ induced by the $F\pi_j$ is then an isomorphism on every $W$, hence an isomorphism of abelian sheaves compatible with the projections, and $(F\Lambda,(F\pi_j)_j)$ is a limit cone of $F\circ M$ in $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal D)$. In particular $F$ preserves the final (zero) object, finite products and kernels (equalizers).

source.place: Modules on Sites, proof of Lemma Tag 04JC ('the exactness of f^{-1} for sheaves of sets implies the exactness of f^{-1} as a functor on abelian sheaves'), with Sites Lemma Tag 00W2 (lemma-limit-sheaf) and Modules on Sites Lemma Tag 03CO (lemma-limits-colimits-abelian-sheaves) for the sectionwise limits

proof.text: *(4) $f^{-1}$ commutes with all colimits, in particular with finite colimits.* By step 1 the abelian $f^{-1}$ is a left adjoint of $f_*$. By [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] (with $L=f^{-1}$, $R=f_*$), for every diagram $M:\mathcal J\to\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ indexed by a small (e.g. finite) category with a colimit cocone $(\Sigma,(\iota_j)_j)$, the cocone $(f^{-1}\Sigma,(f^{-1}\iota_j)_j)$ is a colimit of $f^{-1}\circ M$; colimits of finite diagrams exist in the abelian category $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives]. In particular $f^{-1}$ preserves the initial (zero) object, finite coproducts and cokernels (coequalizers).

source.place: Modules on Sites, Lemma Tag 03DC (lemma-exactness-pushforward-pullback) (2) and its proof (adjoint pair), via Categories Lemma Tag 0038 (lemma-adjoint-exact)

proof.text: *(5) Additivity.* For abelian sheaves $\mathcal G,\mathcal H$ on $\mathcal C$ and morphisms $\varphi,\psi:\mathcal G\to\mathcal H$, the sum is computed sectionwise, i.e. $|\varphi+\psi|=+_{\mathcal H}\circ\langle|\varphi|,|\psi|\rangle$ in $\Sh(\mathcal C)$ [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-algebraic-structures-objects]. Hence, by step 2 and $\lambda_{\mathcal H,\mathcal H}\circ L\langle a,b\rangle=\langle L(\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\langle a,b\rangle),L(\mathrm{pr}_2\circ\langle a,b\rangle)\rangle=\langle La,Lb\rangle$: $|F(\varphi+\psi)|=L(+_{\mathcal H})\circ L\langle|\varphi|,|\psi|\rangle=L(+_{\mathcal H})\circ\lambda^{-1}\circ\langle L|\varphi|,L|\psi|\rangle=+_{F\mathcal H}\circ\langle|F\varphi|,|F\psi|\rangle=|F\varphi+F\psi|$, so $F(\varphi+\psi)=F\varphi+F\psi$ ($|-|$ is faithful). Thus $F$, and by step 2 $f^{-1}$, is additive.

source.place: Sites, Section Tag 00YR, discussion before Proposition Tag 00YV (f^{-1}F defined as the quadruple (f^{-1}F, f^{-1}+, f^{-1}0, f^{-1}i))

proof.text: *(6) Kernels, cokernels and exact sequences.* Let $\varphi:\mathcal G\to\mathcal H$ in $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$, an abelian category [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives]. A kernel of $\varphi$ is an equalizer of $\varphi$ and $0$, a cokernel a coequalizer of $\varphi$ and $0$; since $f^{-1}$ is additive (step 5), $f^{-1}(0)=0$, so by steps 3 (with step 2) and 4 $f^{-1}(\ker\varphi\to\mathcal G)$ is a kernel of $f^{-1}\varphi$ and $f^{-1}(\mathcal H\to\operatorname{coker}\varphi)$ a cokernel of $f^{-1}\varphi$. A short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal A\xrightarrow{\alpha}\mathcal B\xrightarrow{\beta}\mathcal E\to0$ means that $\alpha$ is a kernel of $\beta$ and $\beta$ a cokernel of $\alpha$; so its image is short exact. For a sequence $\mathcal A\xrightarrow{\alpha}\mathcal B\xrightarrow{\beta}\mathcal E$ with $\beta\alpha=0$, exactness at $\mathcal B$ means that the canonical monomorphism $\operatorname{Im}\alpha=\ker(\operatorname{coker}\alpha)\to\ker\beta$ (the unique morphism over $\mathcal B$) is an isomorphism; $f^{-1}$ carries $\ker(\operatorname{coker}\alpha)$ to $\ker(\operatorname{coker}f^{-1}\alpha)$ and $\ker\beta$ to $\ker f^{-1}\beta$, both as subobjects of $f^{-1}\mathcal B$, and the canonical morphism to $f^{-1}$ of the canonical morphism (by uniqueness), so $f^{-1}$ of an isomorphism is the canonical morphism for $f^{-1}\alpha,f^{-1}\beta$, which is therefore an isomorphism. Applying this at every place, $f^{-1}$ carries every exact sequence, finite or infinite (e.g. $0\to\mathcal A\to\mathcal I^0\to\mathcal I^1\to\cdots$), to an exact sequence. Together with steps 3 and 4 (finite limits, finite colimits) and 5 (additivity) this is the statement.
